lawyer:
Mr. Sasti Sarker, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners 
Mr. Md. Osman Ghani Bhuiyan, Advocate ----- For the opposite parties
parties:
Md. Kalam Molla and others ----- Plaintiff-petitioners
Vs
Sheikh Samsu and others ----- Defendant-opposite parties
full_judgment:
Mr. A.N.M. Bashir Ullah J:- This Rule, on an application under Section 115 (I) of 
the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the CPC) filed by the plaintiff-petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos.1-15 to show cause as to why judgment and decree dated 06.01.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2" Court, Faridpur, in Title Appeal No.201(A) of 2005 allowing the appeal and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 27.09.2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur, in Title Suit No.120 of 1998 decreeing the suit, should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. By this Rule the legality and propriety of the judgment and decree dated 6.12008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd  Court, Faridpur, in Title Appeal No.201 of 2005 has been challenged. The said title appeal arose out of title suit no.120 of 1998 and the said original suit has been witnessing its fifth judgment after filing of the suit on 16.7.1998.The first judgment in the suit was pronounced by the trial Court decreeing the suit on 23.9.1999 and as against the said judgment title appeal being no.2I3 of 1999 was preferred and the appellate Court below by its judgment dated 23.10.2002 sent the suit back on remand for trial afresh and accordingly the suit was again decreed by its 3' judgment dated 27.9.2005 and against that judgment the contesting defendants preferred title appeal no. 201 of 2005 in the Court of District Judge, Faridpur and the learned Joint District Judge. 2' Court, Faridpur as appellate Court allowed the appeal dismissing the suit by its judgment dated 6.1.2008 (4i and impugned judgment). The plaintiff-petitioners against that judgment moved this Court and obtained the present Rule and thus in disposing the present Rule the suit has been witnessing its fifth judgment. 3r The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the present -petitioners 
as plaintiffs filed title suit no.120 of 1998 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur for declaration of their title into .29 acres of land. Later on through amendment the plaintiffs also sought the declaration that the ex-parte-decree dated 08.7.1993 passed in title suit no.629 of 1981 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur is illegal and non binding upon them averring inter alia that .14 acres of land appertaining to RS plot no.137, 200 and 203 of RS khatian no.35 and .l5 acres of land appertaining to RS plot no. 137, 200 and 203 of RS khatian no. 36 originally belonged to Akiluddin Molla and the said land has been correctly recorded in his name. The plaintiffs are the heirs and successive heirs of Akiluddin Mona. The plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land from the time of their predecessor of Akiluddin Molla and the defendants have no right, title, interest and possession into the suit land.

4. The plaintiffs are the men of simple and credulous nature and they are from a remote village of the country who have no up to date knowledge about the management and preparation of the record of right. Late plaintiff no. 1 Chand Molla was entrusted with the preparation of the record of right in the name of the plaintiffs in the SA record of right and to that end he gave the required data to the concerned officials and he was in believe that the SA record has been prepared and published in the name of the plaintiffs but at the Iln.il stage of the SA record of right the late plaintiff Chand Molla became sick and the other plaintiffs were not proper person to take care of the same. But while the plaintiffs were in peaceful possession of the suit land, all on a sudden in the first part of the month of the Boishakh 1405 BS, the defendant nos. 1 -5 denied the title of the plaintiffs into the suit and and also disclosed that the SA record of right has been prepared in the name of their predecessor, Nazir Sheik in SA khatian no.129 although the defendants had no right, title, interest and possessing into the suit land. 

5. The further case of the plaintiffs is that Akiluddin Molla did never orally settle the suit land to Nazir Sheikh on 15'1' Baishak 1354 BS and Akiluddin Molla did never receive rents on 30th Baishak of the same year from the said Nazir Sheikh the said Nazir  Sheikh was never inducted into the possession of the suit land. The defendant no.3 has no homestead on the land of plot no200 and the defendant no.11 also has no homestead on the land of plot no.203 and it is fact that the Union Parisad erected road taking earth from the suit land with the permission of the plaintiffs and there are roads on the suit land. 

6. The further case of the plaintiffs is that Akiluddin Mona did not exchange .16 acres of land of RS plot no.200 with Ansaruddin Molla, the predecessor of defendant nos.24- 28 (though in the plaint this defendants have been mentioned emmeously as defendant rios.29-33). Akiluddin Molla did not get .05 acres of land from plot no.204 of RS khatian no.42 and 43 and he did never give .16 acres of land from plot no.200 of RS khatian no.35 and 36 to the said Ansaruddin Molla. The plaintiffs had no any knowledge about the title suit no.629 of 1981 or its ex-parte-decree. The summons and the other process of the said suit were never served upon the plaintiffs or their predecessor in interest. The summons and process of the said suit have been suppressed upon the plaintiffs thereafter the plaintiffs of that suit obtained a fraudulent ex-parte-decree on 08.7.1993. So the said decree is not binding upon the plaintiffs. Since the defendants have denied the title of the plaintiffs into the suit land in the first part of the month of Boishak 1405 BS, hence the suit. 

7. The suit was contested by 2 sets of defendants. In one set there was the defendant nos.l-5 and 7-16 while in another set there was the defendant nos.24-28. The defendants no.1 -5 and 7-16 filing written statements denied the material allegation made in the plaint and also claimed that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and the plaintiffs have no cause of action for the suit. The case of the these defendants, in short, is that all the plaintiffs named in the plaint did not file the suit. Md. Kalam Molla. the son of the late plaintiff no. 1 Chand Mollah at the instance of some enemy of the defendants filed the suit to cause harm and mischief to the defendants. The house of the plaintiff nos.1-9 and 13 are far away from the suit land. 

8. The further case of the defendants is that it is fact that Akiluddin Molla was the recorded tenant' of the suit land and his name has been correctly recorded in RS khatian no.35 and 36. Akiluddin Molla was a land and who settled the suit land to Nazir Sheikh. the predecessor of the defendants on 15th Boishak, 1354 BS and he received the rents from Nazir Sheikh on 30th, Baishakh of the same year executing dakhilas. Nazir Sheikh was inducted into the possession of the suit land and he has been cultivating the same by his own plough. Nazir Sheikh had his own land adjacent to the suit plot who died leaving the defendant nos.1-17. The defendant no.3 has homestead on the land of plot no.20 I now he has extended his homestead in to the land of suit plot no. 200 and for the last 16 years he has been possessing the same. The defendant no.11 has been possessing the land of plot no. 203 erecting but thereon. The defendants and the local union parisad have collected earth from the suit land creating some ditch thereon. The suit land has been correctly recorded in the name of Nazir Sheikh in SA khatin no. 129. So, the suit of the plaintiffs is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

9. The defendant nos.24-28 through their written statements denying the material allegations of the plaint averred that the land of RS khatian no. 35 and 36 originally belonged to Akiluddin Molla while .05 acres. of land of RS plot no. 204 of RS khatian no. 42 and 43 belonged to Ansaruddin Molla, the predecessor of the defendant nos. 24-28. Before the RS record of right Akiluddin Malta exchanged .16 acres of land of plot no. 200 with .05 acres of land of plot no. 204 belonged to Ansaruddin Molla and accordingly in the in RS khatian no. 35 and 36 and also in RS khatian no. 42 and 43 there is the reference of the said exchange. In the SA record of right the said land was not recorded correctly in the name of Ansaruddin Mollah and as such the present defendants filed title suit no.629 of 1981 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur and the said suit was decreed ex-parte on 8.7.1983. The defendants of that suit though were served with the notice and summons of that suit but they did not appear in the suit. The decree of that suit is not fraudulent. These defendants have been possessing the land of RS plot no. 200. So, the Rule is liable to be discharged with cost. 

10. Upon the above pleadings, the trial Court framed as many as 6 issues to dispose 
of the suit. The plaintiffs examined 3 witnesses while defendant nos. 1-5/7-16 examined 7 witnesses and the defendant nos. 24-28 examined I witness and the plaintiffs and the defendants filed some documentary evidences which have been duly marked as exhibits in the suit. The trial Court on considered of evidence and other materials on record decreed the suit holding that the plaintiffs have right, title, interest and possession into the suit. The contesting defendant nos.I-5/7-16 being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree of the trial Court preferred title appeal no. 20I(A) of 2005 in the Court of District Judge, Faridpur which has been ultimately heard by the Joint District Judge. 2nd  Court, Faridpur who by his impugned judgment dated 6.1.2008 allowed the appeal setting aside the judgment of the trial Court. The plaintiff-petitioners being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree of the appellate Court below moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

11. Mr. Sash Sarker, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners supports the Rule. He submits that both the trial Court and appellate Court below concurrently found the title of the plaintiffs into the suit land. They very categorically and significantly held that Akiluddin Molla was the owner of the suit land and the suit land was correctly recorded in his name in RS khatian nos. 35 and 36 and Akiluddin Mollah did not settle the suit land orally to Nazir Sheikh in 1354 BS and Akiluddin Molla did not exchange .16 acres of land of plot no. 200 with Ansaruddin Molla, the predecessor of defendant nos. 24-28 and this concurrent findings of Courts below are based on the proper assessment of the materials on record. So this concurrent
findings and decisions of the Courts below did not call for any interference from this Court. 

12. He next submits that the trial Court on a meticulous perusal and scanning of the evidence on record found the possession of the plaintiffs into the suit land but the appellate Court below on some erroneous view found that the plaintiffs have no possession into the suit land. The appellate Court below mis-constructed the evidence of P.Ws 1, 2 and 3. Both the PWs 2 and 3 categorically asserted that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. PW 3 did not give any evidence that he did not know the suit land or he did not know as to who has been possessing the suit land but the appellate Court below on some misreading of evidence of PW 3 mis-constructed his evidence and thereby came to a wrong finding that the P.W 3 did not know the suit land and did not know as who has been possessing the suit land. Both the PWs 2 and 3 have homestead contiguous to the suit land and this fact has not been denied by the defendants at trial. So the PWs 2 and 3 are very much competent witnesses to prove the possession of the plaintiffs. 

13. He also submits that the DWs 2, 3 and 4 have deposed to prove the possession of the defendant nos. 1-17, but none of them could have stated from when the defendants have been possessing the suit land so their such evidence is not credible at all to prove the possession of the defendants. 

14. He also submits that it is fact that the defendants have their homestead adjacent to the suit land and the local witnesses being misconceived of the said fact considered their such possession as possession of the suit land. 

15. He also submits that both the defendant nos.1-17 and 24-28 have been claiming their possession into the suit land and this sort of claim is sufficient to hold that neither the defendant nos. 1-17 nor the defendant nos. 24-28 have been possessing the suit land, rather it is the plaintiffs who have been possessing the suit and continuously from the time of their predecessor-in-interest Akiluddin Molla. There is no case in the hands of the defendants to show that the plaintiffs or their predecessor were ever dispossessed from the suit land at any point of time. More so, the plaintiffs have the right, title and interest into the suit land, so the evidence of possession must be considered with the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs into the suit land but the appellate Court below on some erroneous view found possession of the defendants.

16. As to the Advocate commissioner's report he submits that the report itself reveals that the commissioner did not find any fixed pillar or point for an accurate measurement and thereupon he started his measurement at his own discretion from the plot 199. So this type of measurement cannot be considered as genuine and fair. So the Advocate commissioner's report is not acceptable at all. 

17. He lastly submits that the appellate Court below on the wrong assessment of the evidence and other materials or record held that the plaintiffs have no possession into the suit land but this findings is not based on materials on record, as such, he has committed an error of fact as well as law occasioning failure of justice to the plaintiff-petitioners. So, the judgment of the appellate Court below is liable to be set aside making the Rule absolute.

18. On the other hands, Mr. Md. Osman Ghani Bhuiya, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party nos. 1-15 opposes the Rule. He submits that the suit was not maintainable as the plaintiffs have no possession into the suit land. The appellate Court below relying on the materials on record came to a correct conclusion that the plaintiffs have no possession into the suit land. So the suit is hit under the proviso of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. 

19. He also submits that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession into the suit land while the defendants by sufficient and cogent evidence could have proved their possession. He referring the Advocate commissioner's report exhibit-A submits that the Advocate Commissioner found the structures and various trees on the suit land and those structures and trees belonged to the defendants. The Commissioner also found ditch in the suit land as the defendants collected earth from the said ditch. Since the suit land is not plain now, as asserted, by the plaintiffs there is no scope for them to cultivate the land as plain land and the commissioner's report have supported the defendant's case that they have been possessing the suit land making structures thereon and also planting various type of trees into the suit land and the appellate Court below on the proper assessment of evidence and other materials on record found the possession of the defendants and rightly dismissed the suit. So, the judgment of the appellate Court below did not call for interference from this Court. So the Rule is liable to he discharged with cost. 

20. I have considered the above arguments and submissions of the learned Advocates of 
Sheikh Sam. & Ors (A.N.M. Bashir Ullah, J)325 both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record. 

21. On going to the materials on record it is found that it is almost admitted that the land of RS khatian no.35 and 36 originally belonged to Akiluddin Molla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs. But the case of the plaintiffs is that Akiluddin Molla did never settle the suit land to Nazir Sheikh while the case of the contesting defendant nos. 1-5 and 7-16 is that Akiluddin Molla orally settled the suit land in the first part of Boishakh 1354 BS to Nazir Sheikh, the predecessor of these of defendants and took rents from the Nazir Sheikh executing the dakhila on 30, Baishak of [354 BS. 

22. The case of the another set of defendants namely the defendant nos. 24-28 is that Akiluddin Molla exchanged .16 acres of land from the land of plot no. 200 with Ansaruddin Molla, the predecessor of defendant nos. 24-28 and in the said exchange Akiluddin Molla got .05 acres of land from the land of plot no. 204 from Ansaruddin Molla. 

23. The trial Court and the appellate Court below concurrently found that the right, title and interest which was available in favour of Akiluddin Molla at the time of preparation of RS record of right has not been extinguished in any way and both the Courts below also concurrently found that Akiluddin Molla did never settle the suit land to Nazir Sheikh nor exchanged with Ansaruddin Mona. The relevant findings of the appellate Court below runs in the following manner: 
“এমতাবস্থায় আনজিন তপাসিল বর্ণিত নালিশী জমিতে অখিলউদ্দিন মোল্ল্যার স্বত্ব অটুট থাকা প্রতিষ্টিত হয় এবং তাহার নিকট হইতে উক্ত সম্পত্তিতে ওয়ারিশসূত্রে ও ক্রমওয়ারিশসূত্রে বাদীগণের স্বত্ব অর্জিত হইয়াছে মর্মে উপরোক্ত আলোচনার মাধ্যমে প্রতিপন্ন হয়। অর্থাত আরজির তপসিল বর্ণিত নালিশী জমিতে বাদীপক্ষের দাবীমত স্বত্ব অর্জনের বিষয়টি যথাযথ বলিয়া প্রমাণ হয়।”

" From the above findings, it appears that the appellate Court below found the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs into the suit land. The trial Court decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs finding the right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiffs into the suit land. In the case of Abdul Kader Vs. Noor Mohammad, 36 DLR(AD) 261 it has been held that the findings of the Courts below on the basis of no evidence is of no legal consequence and the finding, of the Courts below could be disturbed if there is any misreading of the evidence or misconstruction of the evidence. In the case of 16 BLD (AD) 197 it has been held that the revisional Court may interfere in the concurrent findings of the facts of the Courts below when there appears misreading of evidence, wrong appreciation of evidence, non-consideration of oral and documentary evidence by the Courts below and when the findings of the Courts below are found to be perverse and not based on the evidence on record which resulted in to an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. In the Case of Abdul Gafur Vs. Md. Abdur Razzak 62 DLR (AD) 242 it was held that the revisional Court cannot reverse the concurrent findings of the Courts below based on proper appreciation of the evidence on record. 

24. Now, the preponderant views emerged from the above referred decisions is that if the concurrent findings of the Courts below are based on proper appreciation of the evidence on record, the some cannot be disturbed, but if the concurrent findings are based on the misreading of evidence, wrong appreciation of evidence and non-consideration of oral and documentary evidence by the Courts below, the findings and decisions of the Courts below can be disturbed. Now, let us considered whether the concurrent findings of the Courts below as to the title of the plaintiffs into the suit land suffers from any misreading or non-reading and misconstruction of evidence. 

25. From the materials on record it appears that the I" set of defendants could not adduce any evidence in order to prove the oral settlement of Nazir Sheikh. They asserted in their pleadings that Akiluddin Molla received rents from Nazir Sheikh executing rent receipts. DW I Md. Samsul Hug in his cross-examination stated in the following ways:
“আমি মালেক প্রদত্ত দাখিলা্ আদালতে দাখিল করিয়াছি। আমার দাখিলী দাখিলায় কোন দাগ নম্বর খতিয়ান নম্বর এবং জমির পরিমান উল্লেখ নাই। দাখিলায় মৌজার নামও উল্লেখ নাই।”

For the reasons stated above the said dakhilas have not been marked as exhibit in the suit by the trial Court. But from the very nature of dakhila it appears that the same did not bear the plot and khatian number and the quantity of land. This type of dakhila cannot be the genuine dakhila to show the payment of rents. In fact the set of defendants could not adduce an iota of evidence in support of their such oral settlement. 

In the S.A. record of right, the suit land has been recorded in the name of defendants in S.A. khatian no.I29, but it is very much settled now that the record of right is not the document of title of any land rather the parties are to show the basis of the said record of right but the defendants could not show any basis of the said SA record of

26. On the other hand, the defendant nos. 24-28 in their written statements could not even mention the date of alleged exchange. There is nothing in the evidence of DW 8 as to the prove of the said exchange, as such, both the Courts below rightly disbelieved the settlement in favour of Nazir Sheikh as well as the alleged exchange between Akiluddin Motto and Ansaruddin Molla. In the result, I am of the sharp view that the findings and decisions of the Courts below as to the right and title of the plaintiffs into the said land are based on proper appreciation of the evidence and materials on record which calls for no interference from this Court. 

27. The appellate Court below though found the title of the plaintiffs into the suit land but ultimately dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiffs have no possession into the suit and and the plaintiffs did not challenge the decree of title suit no.629 of 1981.

28. It is fact that in the prayer portion of the plaint there appears no prayer as against the said title suit but the plaintiffs amended the plaint seeking relief against the said title suit in following terms and condition. The plaintiffs amended the plaint (ding a petition in the trial Court on 16.9.2003 where the relief against the said title suit was sought for in the following manner: 
উক্ত ৬২৯/১৯৮১ মোকদ্দমার ৮/৭/১৯৯৩ তারিখের একতরফা রায় ও ১৪/৭/১৯৯৩ তারিখের একতরফা ডিক্রি সম্পীর্ন অবৈধ বেআইনী যোগাযোগী ও অকার্যকরী রুল এন্ড ভয়িড ও কাগজের কারবার হইতেছে মাত্র েএবং উক্তরুপ ডিক্রি দ্বারা এই বাদী পক্ষ আদৌ বাধ্য নহে।”

In my consideration this sort of prayer should have been incorporated into the prayer portion of the suit but the same has not been done at all, as such, the appellate Court below high lighting the wanting of the same into the prayer portion held that the plaintiffs did not seek any relief as against the decree of the former title suit. 

In the case of Zamiruddin Ahmed Vs. Ziaul Haque and other, 49 DLR 622 it was held that party must not suffer for the bad pleading of the mufussil Court. In the said case this Court observed in the following ways: 

"Hence I feel inclined to observe that the pleading is not happy but the party must not suffer for confused and bad pleading. Law is settled that it is the substance and not the form of the plaint which at is to be looked and considered and Mufussil Court's pleadings are to be construed liberally" 

The plaintiffs though sought the relief as against the decree of the former suit but the said was not incorporated in the prayer portion of the suit but for any reason the relief was sought for within averment of the plaint and same also should have not been over looked by the appellate Court below. 

29. The plaintiffs claimed in the suit that the summons and process of the former suit had not been served upon them and the plaintiffs of that suit had suppressed the process and summons upon the defendants (plaintiffs of the present suit) of that suit and they practicing fraud upon the Court obtained a fraudulent decree. But the defendant nos. 24-28 did not take any earnest effort to address this allegation and they did not try to prove that the summons and process of that suit were served upon the defendants of that suit and no fraud was practiced upon the Court in obtaining the decree in that suit. So, in my consideration the appellate Court 

30. Now, corning to the question of possession of the parties, it appears that the appellate Court below disbelieved the evidence of PW I in regards to the possession as he could not say the plot numbers of the adjacent land of the suit land. He also disbelieved the evidence of P.W2 as he said that the suit land is possessed neither by the plaintiffs nor by the defendants and the land is fallen vacant as un-cultivated land. He also disbelieved the evidence of PW3 as he could not say the name of the mouja of the suit land but at the same time from the judgment of appellate Court below it is found that he did not rely on the evidence of defendants to ascertain the possession of the defendants. 

31. It is very natural and probable that P.W1 as one of the plaintiff will assert their possession in to the suit land, but from the evidence of PW2 who has homestead adjacent to the suit land it is found that he categorically stated that he had borga cultivated the land of plot no. 200 but for the last 2 years the land has been fallen vacant uncultivated. In cross-examination he categorically stated that he has the homestead in the northern side of the land of plot no. 200. This evidence or fact has not been denied by the defendants. So, PW2 is a very competent witness to tell anything about the possession of the suit land. 

32. More so, from the materials on record it transpires that PW 2 has given very truth and genuine evidence in the trial Court as to the present position of the suit land. PW 2 stated that at present for the last two years the land remains uncultivated and the same fact has been described by the DWs 2. 3 and 4 who have come in the Court to prove the possession of the defendants. Now, if the suit land or a portion thereof remains uncultivated for the last 2 or 3 years, by this fact, the persons who have title and interest into the snit land cannot he said to be out of possession or has been ousted from the suit land. 

PW3 Sheikh Khali! testified that he has homestead contiguous to the suit land and plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. From the cross-examination of the defendants it appears that PW3 is the relation of the defendants but their appears no suggestion that for any internal clique or for any other reason he has deposed falsely. Since the PW3 is also a contiguous land holder of the suit land, so he is a competent witness to depose as to the possession of the parties into suit land. From the materials on record it appears that both the P.Ws 2 and 3 are independent and disinterested witnesses and there appears no earthly reason to disbelieve them or to discard their unblemished and noted evidence in the Court. Since the title of the plaintiffs were found into the suit land, so the evidence of PWs 2 and 3 as to their possession into the suit land is consistent with the findings of the title of the plaintiffs. In this regard I can also rely upon the decision of the case of Erfan Ali Vs Joynal Abedin Mia, 35 DLR (AD) 217, where in it has been held that possession generally follows the title. The title of the plaintiffs were concurrently found by the Courts below, so the legitimate, rational and judicious conclusion would be that the plaintiff have been possessing the suit land pursuant to their such title. 

33. The defendant 110n. 1-5 and 7-16 had asserted their title in to the suit land on the
basis of oral settlement which has been found as a down right false hood, so their possession can not be considered on the basis of the said oral settlement. The defendants could not assert their beginning time and the date of possession, that is, from when they started to possess the suit land. D.Ws 2,3 and 4 have deposed to prove the possession of the defendants but in cross-examination all of them said that they did not know from when the defendants have been possessing the suit land. In fact the evidence of DWs 2, 3, 4 in respect of possession of the defendants do not tally with the materials on record. 

34. In this suit there is a local investigation held by DW 7 Advocate S.M. Al Mamun Hossain. He testified that he held the local investigation of the suit land and he submitted a report, marked exhibit-A. On a careful scrutiny of the said exhibit-A there appears sometimes in the following ways:
“নালীশী দাগের পার্শ্ববর্তী কোন স্থানে নকশা বা সরেজমিনে কোন সীমানা পিলার না থাকায় পক্ষগণের সনাক্তমতে বেনালিশী ১৯৯ দাগের উত্তর-পশ্চিমের কোন হইতে পরিমাপ কার্য শুরু করি।”
 
From the above statements of the report it is clear that the commissioner did not find any fixed pillar for the starting point of the measurement and it is known to everyone that for an accurate measurement and also for an unerring location of the suit land, the measurement must be started from a fixed pillar. Since the commissioner could not ascertain any fixed pillar, the starting of measurement from a certain place cannot be considered as fair and genuine. If for the sake of argument, it is conceded for a moment that he found tress and machan of bottle gourd or other trees into the land of plot nos. 200 and 2003 that does not mean that the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit land. From the materials on record it appears that the suit land is very much adjacent to the land of the defendants. Both the defendant nos. 3 and 11 have been living in the adjacent land of suit plot no, 200 and 203 and as such it was easier for them to claim their possession into the suit land but the fact remains that there is no reason for them to possess the suit land. So, the appellate Court below on the wrong assessment and misconstruction of the evidence on record found the possession of the defendants and thereby came to a wrong conclusion that the plaintiffs have no possession in to the suit land. The appellate Court below was not at all justified to find the possession of the defendants relying on the evidence on record, as such, I find merit in the Rule. 

35. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The judgment of the appellate Court below dated 6:1.2008 passed by the Joint District Judge 2' Court, Faridpur in title appeal no. 201(A) of 2005 is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree of the trial Court dated 27.9.2005 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur in title suit no.120 of 1998 is hereby restored with some modification that the title of the plaintiffs in to the suit land is hereby declared and decree of title suit no.629 of 1981 of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur is declared illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs so far as it relates to the suit land of the plaintiffs. Considering all I pass no order as to cost. 

36. Let a copy of this judgment and order along with the lower Courts record be sent down to the concerned Court for information and necessary action.

End.
